name: Cress
grown_as: Garden cress, 'Plain' in William's records, sown thickly indoors and cut as seedlings about 5 cm tall; it can also be grown on to a full plant.
habit: As a crop, a dense green mat of thin pale stems topped with seed leaves. Grown on, an upright, branched, hairless annual 20 to 60 cm, slender, grey-green.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate; a loose rosette at first
leaf.type: Lower leaves divided once or twice into narrow lobes (pinnately cut); upper stem leaves simple
leaf.outline: Lower leaves 5 to 10 cm, cut into narrow, oblong to strap-like lobes; upper leaves narrow and strap-shaped, 2 to 4 cm
leaf.base: Lower leaves narrowing into a long stalk; upper leaves stalkless
leaf.margin: Lobes smooth or with a few teeth; upper leaves smooth
leaf.veins: A midrib, one vein into each lobe
leaf.stalk: Long on the lower leaves, none on the upper

flower.form: A tiny cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.centre: Six (sometimes fewer) tiny stamens with yellow anthers
flower.behind: Four small green sepals, often with white edges
flower.carried: In crowded spikes at the tips of the stems, lengthening as they flower

fruit: Small, flat, round to oval pods 5 to 6 mm with a narrow wing round the top and a small notch at the tip, held upright and pressed close to the stem on curved stalks; two seeds in each. Green drying straw-brown. Seeds oblong, 2 to 3 mm, red-brown, slimy when wet.
seedling: Two seed leaves, each deeply cut into three lobes like a small trident, on a long thin pale stem; then the first true leaves narrow and toothed.
winter: Nothing: an annual, sown indoors all year for seedlings.

leaf: a lower leaf cut into narrow lobes along a long stalk
upper leaves narrow, strap-shaped and stalkless
bloom: four tiny white spoon-shaped petals in a cross
seedling: two seed leaves each cut into three lobes
young: a small rosette of narrowly lobed leaves
the three-lobed seed leaves still at the base
crop: a dense mat of thin pale stems about 5 cm tall
each topped by a pair of three-lobed seed leaves
flower: a slender upright branched plant with narrow upper leaves
seedhead: small flat round notched pods pressed upright against the stem

look_alikes: Mustard seedlings (sold with cress) have broad kidney-shaped seed leaves, not three-lobed ones. Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) grows in water with leaves of rounded leaflets and long pods. Land cress (Barbarea verna) has glossy lobed leaves and yellow flowers.
